svg.title: RelayHall
svg.desc: Callers — a browser, the CLI, an external harness or automation — reach RelayHall through an optional deployment-owned ingress, which with TLS, DNS, SSO proxies, monitoring, secrets, artifact storage and plugin runtime mounts remains a deployment concern. The RelayHall core is one Compose stack of three services whose host ports bind to 127.0.0.1: a React frontend the browser reaches over same-origin /api and /ws routes, an Express backend holding JWT and principal credentials, REST, OpenAPI, authenticated WebSocket task updates and the plugin proxy, and PostgreSQL 16 holding the authoritative board, identities, credentials, reports, configuration records and audit history. Optional plugins are separate containers with their own manifests and data mounts, reached through the plugin proxy; reporter outposts run next to a harness and push bounded telemetry into the reporting seam; until a reporter is connected, Sessions and Stats show a documented empty state. The core is pull-only: it does not launch, steer, kill or inspect agent runtimes and never mounts harness sessions, transcripts, config, memory or workspace directories; it mounts only its own configuration and data and does not inherit a plugin private runtime access. It stores and serves work, compiles complete task Briefs, and records lifecycle, attribution, dependencies, review history and reports. An external orchestrator pulls authorised state, runs a harness, and writes results back. Theme relay-dark.
